title: API key stall repro + trace notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad capturing commands tried, raw error snippets, theories and short repro notes for the intermittent API-key -> 401 then 429 stall we've been seeing from a small cohort of self-serve accounts. Trying to keep this compact so I can hand it to SRE or product later.

Timeline/high-level summary:
- Issue shows up Nov 2025 in self-serve region us-west-2. Affected customers report a burst of 401s for ~30s, then a stream of 429s (Retry-After sometimes present, sometimes not).
- Pattern: first request(s) after inactivity get 401 (invalid key), immediate retries get 429s. If the user waits ~60s, normal traffic resumes.
- Hypothesis: short-lived per-key auth cache invalidation or a race between key rotation + per-IP rate bucket, or a transient gateway that flips between auth backend and rate limiter.

Notes / reproduction attempts (commands and raw outputs):
1) Basic curl repro from dev laptop (macOS):

curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer rwd_test_ABC123" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-1.5b","input":"hi"}'

Observed: (intermittent)
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json
Date: Tue, 12 Nov 2025 20:14:03 GMT

{"error":{"message":"invalid API key","type":"authentication_error"}}

- Immediate retry (same command) -> sometimes 429:
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 30
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":{"message":"rate limit exceeded","type":"rate_limit_error","retry_after":30}}

2) Repro with Authorization header split vs single header (trying to rule out header parsing issues):
- Done both: Authorization: Bearer rwd_test_ABC123 and Authorization:Bearer rwd_test_ABC123 (no difference).

3) Repro from a different IP (mobile hotspot) -> same sequence, but sometimes only 401s for ~20s then clears. Suggests not strictly per-client-IP on the first error.

4) Increase client backoff / exponential retry (client library)
- With exponential backoff (0.5s,1s,2s,4s) the client recovers, but user-visible latency is bad.

5) Repro against staging (with auth proxy disabled) -> no 401/429 observed. Indicates problem lives in production auth or rate-limiter stack.

Logs / traces captured (examples):
- Request-id: rq_j8f3k9 (user complaint)
  spans:
    - gateway -> auth-validate (200) -> caching layer (miss) -> token-lookup (200) -> success but client still got 401 (race?)
- Another trace rq_k2p9v2
  auth-validate returned 401 from auth-db due to stale cache entry, followed by many 429s from global-rate-limiter that had recorded retries.

Observations from logs: 
- auth-validate occasionally returns 401 for a valid key for a few seconds; the auth-db table shows correct key present, TTL on cache shards shows rapid churn.
- rate-limiter logs show 'burst_count' increment then enter 'throttle' state; the throttle window sometimes set to 30s. Some 429s have explicit Retry-After header, others do not.
- Many affected traces include the same gateway node (gw-usw2-12) -> possibility of one bad instance with corrupted auth cache.

Experiments tried (and results):
- Flushed auth-cache on gw-usw2-12 -> short-term improvement observed for ~5 minutes, then reappeared.
- Toggled feature flag 'use-local-auth-cache' -> disabling local cache removed 401/429 spikes in small A/B test (N=3 users). Strong signal that local cache logic/race caused transient 401 then retries hitting rate-limiter.
- Increased logging on auth-cache miss/hit with correlation id.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Local auth cache staleness + race: a key rotation or administrative change invalidates key in central auth-db but local cache state lags, causing auth-validate to flip between accepted and rejected states across the fleet. Retry storms then push requests into rate-limiter buckets -> 429. (High confidence)
2) Gateway instance-level bug: a specific gateway instance exhibits corrupt cache TTL (observed gw-usw2-12). (Medium confidence)
3) Global rate-limiter bucket keyed incorrectly (e.g., key + IP + route) causing retries after 401 to accumulate in same bucket and trip global throttle quickly. (Medium confidence)
4) Client SDKs hitting rotate-key logic unexpectedly (unlikely; repro from plain curl). (Low confidence)

Immediate mitigation ideas tried and next steps:
- Short term: patch gateway to disable local cache + roll. Did an internal canary -> traffic stable for canary. Plan: rollout across fleet during low-traffic window.
- Mid term: add conservative retry-after on 401 in gateway with small randomized jitter so clients don't hammer immediately (reduce ability to pile into rate-limiter).
- Long term: implement coordinated cache invalidation (pub/sub) for key rotations + hard TTL floor. Add metrics: auth-cache-hit-rate, cache-stale-incidents, per-gateway 401 spikes.

Notes to hand off to SRE:
- Important traces: rq_j8f3k9, rq_k2p9v2. Check gw-usw2-12 logs around 2025-11-12 20:13-20:20 UTC.
- Can recreate locally by toggling local cache TTL to 1s and issuing quick retries; I left a minimal script in my local bin (ping-auth-burst.sh) that reproduces the 401->429 pattern.

Minimal repro script (pseudo):
#!/bin/bash
# rapid-fire 5 requests to simulate retry storm
for i in {1..5}; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{redirect_url}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer rwd_test_ABC123" \
    -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/chat/completions -d '{"model":"rw-1.5b","input":"debug"}' &
  sleep 0.2
done
wait

What I want to hand to product/SRE for next meeting:
- Short playbook: roll gateway patch disabling local cache -> monitor per-gateway 401/429 metrics -> rollback if needed.
- Dashboard: show per-gateway 401 spikes, 429 bursts, Retry-After distribution, and per-key throttle events.
- Customer comms draft: admit transient auth error + mitigation steps, avoid over-technical details.

Open questions / TODOs (my checklist):
- [ ] Confirm whether key rotation flow writes tombstones that might be misinterpreted by local caches.
- [ ] Confirm whether rate-limiter keys include client IP by default and whether that interacts badly with mobile networks.
- [ ] Add deterministic unit test that simulates cache flip from accept->reject->accept under heavy retry and ensure rate-limiter doesn't escalate wrongly.
- [ ] Add a low-cost global metric for "short auth flaps" to catch this earlier.

Notes to self: keep this file short, move polished runbook and playbook into shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/ when we have consensus.

-- Evan
